label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Here's the post. It comes to 398 words and about 2,200 characters, including the hashtags.

---

The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms wrapped up on Saturday, and on behalf of the organising team, I want to thank everyone who made it happen.

From 5 to 7 November, 41 participants (MSc and early PhD students from 9 states) spent three days in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune. We received 112 applications and selected participants on the basis of a statement and one reference.

Thank you to our speakers:
Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad), for the lectures on the Mordell–Weil theorem
Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai), for the lectures on modular forms
Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki, who joined online from Kraków to take us through computations in Sage

One moment I'll remember: an MSc student from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Dr. Iyer's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him in front of the room. Exactly the kind of exchange we hoped for.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for her guidance from the first proposal to the final session. To Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out hostel rooms at 11 pm when a booking went wrong. And to the six PhD students who volunteered as TAs and ran the problem sessions. That format worked really well, and we'll keep it.

The school was supported by a ₹2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative scheme, which covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Not everything went to plan. On day 2, the power went out for nearly two hours and every laptop died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days.

If I take one thing away, it's that small schools like this matter a lot for MSc students, often more than big conferences. In a room of 40, people actually ask their questions.

Slides and problem sheets will be up on the department website within two weeks.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, depending on funding.

Finally, thank you to all 41 participants for the questions, the patience and the energy. And to my co-organisers Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza: we did it.

#NumberTheory #EllipticCurves #ModularForms #Mathematics

---

A few notes:
- I wrote "Dr. Iyer" instead of "Sunanda ma'am" because other departments and outside people will be reading it. If you'd rather keep "ma'am," that's fine too.
- When you post, tag the speakers, Prof. Venkatesan, Ketaki and Faizan. LinkedIn tags replace the plain names, so the word count stays about the same.
- You could also name the Silchar student (with his permission) or tag the six TAs. That would add roughly 10–20 words, so you'd have to cut something to stay under 400.
